instruction:
Reconstruct the final tower described by these successive speech messages from one trial. Later messages can correct earlier ones. A correction that depends on an unseen Builder state may remain ambiguous.

Message 1: Okay, so you want to take a blue block and place it in the top two squares of the grid with the long side facing you. And then on the top left corner, you want to put a red block on top of the blue block and another red block on top of that. So you have an L like this. So two red blocks on top of the horizontal blue block in the top two squares and the red blocks go on the left side. Yeah. Okay. Just checking. Thank you.

assumptions: The blue block's 'long side facing you' was interpreted as the 4-unit dimension being along the x-axis, perpendicular to the viewer, to fit the 'top two squares' (z=[0,2]) constraint. This results in a blue block spanning the entire back row (x=[0,4], z=[0,2]).
The 'top left corner' of the blue block was interpreted as the far-left region (x=[0,2], z=[0,2]), and the red blocks were placed at x=0, z=0 to align with the corner of the grid cell.
